assessment.reason: The projected assist mean sits well below the half-assist line. The case still clears the -185 break-even across the supplied sensitivity band. No sourced blocker targets Podkolzin, but the price is steep and coverage is thin.
assessment.model_case: The model projects about 0.30 assists on 16.6 minutes, median zero, from a 164-game sample. The weakness is deployment: line and power-play role are unverified, and promotion to a scoring line would lift the assist rate more than the tenth-scale sensitivity tests.
assessment.price_case: The main 0.5 line at -185 needs roughly -185 break-even. The model's fair price is near -287 against a market near -188, with only one other book. The 0.1-weight blend leaves a thin cushion, so any price drift erodes it quickly.
assessment.context_case: The Edmonton injury table lists several forwards out, which could reshuffle lines in either direction. Podkolzin's own status and role are unverified, and absence from the table does not establish health.

qualitative_review.countercase: The market implies a meaningfully higher assist rate than the model. With Edmonton forwards out, Podkolzin could draw more ice time or power-play work than the 16.6-minute projection. A heavy -185 price leaves little room if his role rises. Book rules are assumed, not checked.
